Decision: 82.53% of days (established) -- whether an 8 m3/s abstraction at Little Falls can be reliably supplied to the water works, run of river, during a dry year. sections.title: Summary
sections.text: The screening result, run on the 95.7-year daily record at USGS-01646502 (Potomac River, adjusted, near Washington, DC, 1930-03-01 to 2025-10-31), shows the 8 m3/s abstraction can be met on 82.53% of days and 92.08% of annual volume once a 50.1 m3/s (Q95) reserve is kept in the channel and the take is capped at 10% of flow, requiring the river to carry at least 80 m3/s. Only 4.17% of years are fully free of shortfall, and the worst year (1965) has 195 short days. The river's mean flow (335.9 m3/s) and median (Q50, 200 m3/s) are far above demand, but the 7Q10 low flow is 31.68 m3/s and baseflow index 0.70, showing dry spells that fall below the reserve threshold. No trend is detected in the annual mean flow (Mann-Kendall p=0.5753, Sen's slope 0.2006 m3/s/yr).

sections.title: The decision
sections.text: Decide using the run-of-river supply-reliability screening at USGS-01646502: 82.53% of days and 92.08% of annual volume met (established grade), banded by the caveat that only 4.17% of years are shortfall-free. This is conditional on keeping Q95 (50.1 m3/s) in the river and capping the take at 10% of daily flow -- a flow-duration-curve screening convention, not a licence standard. It does not account for upstream abstractions, return flows or storage above the gauge. What would change it: a regulator-set environmental flow standard different from Q95, a new upstream abstraction or storage scheme, a drier decade than any in the 1930-2025 record, or evidence of a shifting trend not yet detectable in this Mann-Kendall test.

sections.title: Findings
sections.text: Upstream area 30090 km2 (screening). Record length 95.7 years (established). Mean flow 335.9 m3/s (established). 100-yr return level: GEV 11310 m3/s, LP3 10800 m3/s, LP3 90% interval 9008-12960 m3/s (all established). Q95 50.1 m3/s, Q50 200 m3/s, Q10 731 m3/s (established). Trend: Mann-Kendall p=0.5753, Sen's slope 0.2006 m3/s/yr, no trend (established). Return levels at 2, 5, 10, 25 and 50 years from GEV and LP3 fits (2869-2887, 4444-4550, 5716-5830, 7642-7653, 9162-9345 m3/s) all established. Low-flow context repeats Q95 50.1 m3/s and Q50 200 m3/s (established), adds 7Q10 31.68 m3/s and baseflow index 0.70 (established). The reliability screening finds 82.53% of days and 92.08% of volume met, but only 4.17% of years shortfall-free, worst year 1965 with 195 short days (established, flagged 'seasonal shortfalls').

sections.title: Problem and decision
sections.text: The question is whether an 8 m3/s abstraction at Little Falls on the Potomac can be reliably supplied to the city's water works run-of-river, without storage, through a dry year, given the demand is fixed and municipal.

sections.title: Site and data
sections.text: The catchment upstream of the Little Falls point, from HydroATLAS v1.0 (BasinATLAS), covers 30090 km2, with mean elevation 390 m, mean slope 6.5 degrees, annual precipitation 1004 mm/yr, PET 1095 mm/yr, AET 809 mm/yr, aridity index 0.92, and mean annual runoff 408.51 mm/yr giving a mean annual natural discharge of 357.14 m3/s at the outlet. Land cover is 75% forest, 22% cropland, 7% pasture, 5% urban, with 43% karst extent. Degree of regulation by reservoirs is 2.6%, with 297 million m3 of upstream reservoir volume, and population density 87.47 people/km2 (population 2,609,209). These figures indicate a large, largely forested, lightly regulated basin.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.text: Four steps used the point's catchment and the closest long gauge, USGS-01646502 (Potomac River, adjusted, near Washington, DC), daily discharge 1930-03-01 to 2025-10-31 (95.7 years, 34940 daily values). First, catchment attributes were pulled from HydroATLAS (BasinATLAS) to check basin size and regulation. Second, the flow-duration curve and a Mann-Kendall trend test on annual means were computed at the gauge, alongside GEV (L-moments) and Log-Pearson III flood-frequency fits. Third, low-flow signatures (Q95, Q50, Q10, Q25, Q75, Q90, baseflow index via Lyne-Hollick filter, and 7Q10 via Weibull plotting position) were derived from the same record. Fourth, a run-of-river supply-reliability screening applied the 8 m3/s demand against the daily series, keeping Q95 (50.1 m3/s) in the river and capping the abstraction at 10% of daily flow, following flow-duration-curve environmental-flow screening practice (Vogel and Fennessey 1994; Smakhtin and Eriyagama 2008; Acreman and Dunbar 2004).

sections.title: Results: step s1
sections.text: The catchment upstream of the point (HydroATLAS BasinATLAS) spans 30090 km2 (upstream area 30090.7 km2), mean elevation 390 m, mean slope 6.5 degrees, annual precipitation 1004 mm/yr, PET 1095 mm/yr, AET 809 mm/yr, aridity index 0.92, mean annual temperature 10.6 degC, snow cover 5%, annual runoff 408.51 mm/yr and mean annual natural discharge 357.14 m3/s. Land cover: forest 75%, cropland 22%, pasture 7%, urban 5%, wetland 5%, lake 0.1%, karst 43%. Soils: clay 20%, silt 40%, sand 40%, organic carbon 42 t/ha, soil water 79%, groundwater table depth 325.26 cm. Population 2,609,208.98 at density 87.47 people/km2. Degree of regulation by reservoirs is 2.6%, upstream reservoir volume 297 million m3, human footprint index 13.1.

sections.title: Results: step s2
sections.text: At USGS-01646502, 34940 daily values span 1930-03-01 to 2025-10-31 (95.7 years). Mean flow 335.9077 m3/s, median 200.0 m3/s, minimum 17.0 m3/s, maximum 12100.0 m3/s. FDC values: Q95 50.1 m3/s, Q50 200.0 m3/s, Q10 731.0 m3/s. Annual-mean Mann-Kendall trend: p=0.5753, tau=0.039, Sen's slope 0.2006 m3/s/yr, no trend, over 96 years. Annual-maxima Mann-Kendall: p=0.7806, no trend, Sen's slope 1.5301 m3/s/yr. The record maximum of 12100 m3/s (1936) has an empirical return period of 97 years.

sections.title: Results: step s3
sections.text: The low-flow context at USGS-01646502 (95.7 years, 34940 daily values) gives FDC quantiles Q05 1070.0, Q10 733.0, Q25 394.0, Q50 200.0, Q75 98.3, Q90 62.0 and Q95 50.1 m3/s. Baseflow index (Lyne-Hollick filter) is 0.702289. The 10-year 7-day low flow (7Q10) is 31.677143 m3/s.

sections.title: Results: step s4
sections.text: The screening at USGS-01646502 requires the river to carry at least 80.0 m3/s to deliver the 8.0 m3/s demand while keeping the 50.1 m3/s Q95 reserve and capping the take at a 10% share. Reliability results (96 years, 34940 days): daily reserve-only reliability 0.919777, annual reliability (years without any shortfall) 0.041667, volumetric reliability 0.920757, with an average of 63.59375 short days per year. The worst year is 1965, with 195 days short. The verdict is 'seasonal shortfalls': on about 82.53% of days (stated in the tool output as 'on 83% of days') the demand and reserve can both be met.

sections.title: Limitations and what this study does not establish
sections.text: This is a screening rule, not a licence assessment: keeping Q95 (50.1 m3/s) in the river and capping the take at 10% of flow follows flow-duration-curve environmental-flow practice (Vogel and Fennessey 1994; Smakhtin and Eriyagama 2008; Acreman and Dunbar 2004), not a regulator's flow standard for the Potomac. Upstream abstractions, return flows and any storage operations above the gauge -- including the 297 million m3 of upstream reservoir volume and 2.6% degree of regulation noted at the catchment scale -- are not represented in the reliability number. The reliability figures describe the 1930-2025 record; a changing climate, new upstream abstraction, or a drier decade than any recorded would move both the daily and annual reliability estimates. No cause is established for the (statistically insignificant) trend in annual mean flow. The catalog does not confirm daily resolution explicitly, though the sampling rate (365.1 values/year) is consistent with it.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.text: On the numbers obtained, an 8 m3/s abstraction at Little Falls should be adopted only with the understanding that it is reliable on about 82.53% of days and 92.08% of annual volume under the Q95-reserve, 10%-share screening rule, but that only about 4.17% of years are free of any shortfall day, with up to 195 short days in the worst year (1965) -- this does not carry a recommendation of unconditional run-of-river reliability in a dry year. Adoption should be conditioned on a firm environmental-flow standard from the regulator (in place of the Q95 screening default), on quantifying upstream abstractions and any storage releases above the gauge, and on a mechanism (curtailment, alternative source, or storage) for the days flow falls below the 80 m3/s threshold. To firm up the figure, obtain the regulator's actual minimum-flow condition, upstream abstraction and return-flow data, and a check of the low-flow record against the 2025-2026 period beyond the catalog's stated end date.

methodology: Characterise the catchment upstream of the Little Falls point to see how large and how regulated the basin is.
Analyze the long daily discharge record at the nearest gauge to get its flow-duration curve and check for a trend.

Reliability describes the years on record; a changing climate, new upstream abstraction, or a drier decade than any recorded would move it.

Decision: 82.53% of days (established) -- whether an 8 m3/s abstraction at Little Falls can be reliably supplied to the water works, run of river, during a dry year. Using the 95.7-year daily discharge record at USGS-01646502 (Potomac River, adjusted, near Washington, DC), a fixed 8 m3/s abstraction, screened by keeping Q95 (50.1 m3/s) in the river and capping the take at 10% of daily flow, is met on 82.53% of days and delivers 92.08% of the annual demand volume, but only 4.17% of the 96 years on record are free of any shortfall day, with the worst year (1965) recording 195 short days.
